newsitem.title: JORDAN: Amman shares dip slightly in steady trade.
newsitem.headline: Amman shares dip slightly in steady trade.

text.p: Jordan's stock exchange dipped slightly on Sunday in moderate trade focused on a handful of select blue chips in mostly local speculative buying, brokers said.
The official 60-share Amman Financial Market (AFM) index shed 0.02 percent to 159.49 points in turnover of 791,563 dinars ($1.1 million).
Again the bourse appeared to be underpinned by activity on the same market favourites, in what was described as mostly speculative trade.
Brokers said they suspected orders came from small and medium-sized local funds which are pinning hopes on another buying spree by foreign funds.

Last month global fund purchases helped push prices to their highest levels in over two years, encouraging local funds to sell some of their holdings after prices rose as high as eight percent in a span of two weeks on some blue chips.
But since the start of the month the market has again fallen as global demand petered out.
Jordan Cement Factories dominated the day's volume but shed 0.02 dinars to 4.05 dinars in healthy 318,189 dinars turnover, nearly half the session's volume.
Two other mining stocks, Jordan Phosphate Mines and Arab Potash again were among the busiest traded stocks with mostly local funds behind the deals, brokers said.
The former was unchanged at 4.00 dinars and the other rose 0.02 dinars to 6.62 dinars in 88,000 dinars and 93,334 dinars of trade respectively.
There was some activity on Jordan-Kuwait Bank, which had a large 1.4 million share deal worth around $6 million executed on Saturday on behalf of a Bahrain-based bank.
"The buyers were a Bahrain bank with Kuwaiti investors," said broker Abdul-Mutaleb Abu-Hijlah.
Kuwaiti shareholders who already own a minority stake in the Jordanian bank are rumoured to have been behind the bloc deal which involved Jordanian investors who held sizeable holdings.
Brokers linked the second day of buying to a power struggle between the boards of Jordan-Kuwait and Bank of Jordan over the control of the former bank.

Analysts say Bank of Jordan, which already has a significant stake in the bank, has set its sights on taking control but is being resisted by the board of Jordan-Kuwait Bank, which has been lobbying support from some shareholders.
Overall 13 shares fell, nine rose and 11 traded but closed unchanged.
The private Pearl Index of the 45 best-performing shares in terms of turnover and financial performance rose 0.02 percent to 81.79 points, 1.92 percent down from the start of the year.
